In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GMP addition to EPS foam forces the conductive– radiative heat transfer mechanism to change.
the addition of GMP to the EPS foam matrix, in the form of a 1–15 μm powder, is a promising approach to reducing its thermal conductivity.

the GMP addition in EPS foam forces the conductive–thermal resistance to increase by 10–15% (depending on the GMP content), while the radiation component decreases by the same amount, which is the main reason for a drop of the total thermal resistance of 20–40% (depending on thickness).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the absence of convection, a small addition of graphite microfillers to the EPS polymer matrix changes the conductive– radiative heat transfer mechanism, which is a new finding.
the EPS foam thermal insulation with 4.3 wt.% of GMP is more than twice as efficient as the “dotted” grey EPS.

, in EPS insulation with GMP, the conductive–thermal conductivity of the matrix is the main contributor to the total thermal conductivity, which is why the total thermal conductivity is lower than that of pure EPS.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the conductive– radiative heat transfer mechanism can be forced to change by a proper addition of GMP in EPS foam, and that the change is mainly due to a drop in the thermal conductivity of the polymer matrix.
the conductive–thermal resistance gain of GMP addition is not a simple linear function of the GMP content.

the GMP addition to EPS foam may force the change in the heat transfer mechanism, which in turn may lead to the reduction of the thermal conductivity and, consequently, of the thickness required to reach a desired level of thermal resistance.
